conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, I'm Dr. Lee. I’ll be taking care of you tonight. Can you tell me what brought you to the hospital?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Hi, Doctor. My left leg has been swelling up for about two weeks. It’s bigger than the right one, and it just feels heavy and tight.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Any pain, redness, or warmth in the leg?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: It’s a little warm, and the skin looks red, especially on the inside of my left shin. There’s some discomfort at the bottom of my feet, but no sharp pain.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Okay. Any fever, chills, or shortness of breath?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No fever. I’m breathing okay on my oxygen. But I did have one quick chest pressure, just for a few seconds, left side. It didn’t come back.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Thanks. We’ll check that, but it doesn’t sound like a heart issue. We did an ultrasound on your legs to check for blood clots.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Was there a clot? I’ve had swelling before, but this feels different.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The scan couldn’t see all the veins clearly because of your body habitus, but we didn’t find any clots in the main veins. So that’s good news.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Oh, okay. So what’s causing the swelling?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It looks like chronic venous insufficiency — that means your leg veins aren’t moving blood back up well. You also have some skin changes and a small area where an ulcer might be starting.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And the redness? That wasn’t there before.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: There’s some pus under the skin on your left leg, and it’s warm — that suggests mild cellulitis, a skin infection. We’re starting you on an antibiotic called Keflex.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will I need to stay long?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll keep you overnight to monitor. Your labs and chest X-ray don’t show heart failure or a serious infection. You’re stable, so we expect to discharge you tomorrow.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. Your labs improved — white count is down, and no signs of heart strain. We’re confident it’s not a heart issue.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: What about my heart rhythm? I remember I have atrial fibrillation.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re not in afib now, but you should be on a blood thinner. Since you don’t want shots, we discussed a pill option like apixaban. We’ll wait for your cardiologist to approve it because you’re already on aspirin.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That makes sense. And my swelling — will the diuretic help?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, your torsemide helps with fluid, but we noticed you haven’t been taking it regularly. That might also explain why you’ve been urinating more lately — it’s a side effect when restarting it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Oh, right. I stop when I feel fine, but then the swelling comes back.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. Try to take it daily, even when you feel okay. Also, compression stockings will help with the leg swelling and prevent ulcers from getting worse.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re getting ready to discharge you. You’ll finish the Keflex for five days total and keep using your regular medications.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And if the sore on my leg opens up?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: If it breaks open, clean it gently, apply a Xeroform dressing with gauze, and wrap it with compression — either Ace wraps or stockings. Your nursing home staff can help.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. And I should keep weighing myself?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, every morning. Call your doctor if you gain more than three pounds in a day — that could mean fluid buildup.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you, Doctor. I’ll try to stay on top of my meds this time.
